title: Jimmy Blanton's greatness and the Dave Dexter review
summary: Lee calls Blanton the top bass player of his time and recounts a bassist's letter rebuking Dave Dexter's DownBeat criticism.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: You mentioned that you were a good friend of Jimmy Blanton's?
Would you tell me a little bit about Jimmy Blanton?

Well, as much as I know about Jimmy Blanton, probably during his time, he was probably -- if you have a 'best' among musicians, and I don't like to use that word, and I don't too much believe in there being a best bass player, best saxophone player, you know, or best trumpet player -- I think excellence can be -- you reach a point, and then you can put them all there together, unless you're talking about a pianist and then a jazz pianist and then Art Tatum.

Now you must put Art Tatum over on the side, but the rest of the musicians, I don't really know, but if it had been a bass player at the time that really, would have been put in that position, I think it would have been Jimmy Blanton.

I remember Dave Dexter reviewed one of the things that Bear did -- we called him Bear because of the record he did, because he made "Jack the Bear", and in this review, Dexter knocked what Blanton was playing, and it's so funny when you really reach a certain point where some other people will take up the fight for you. Blanton and I read it and it didn't mean too much.

But Koetsabiskie (PHONETIC) -- Koetsabiskie wrote and answered Dave Dexter; that's when Dave was writing for the DownBeat. And like it went something like, "How dare you criticize a virtuoso such as Jimmy Blanton. If I had to say anything about the recording that he made, and I have everything he's ever done -- the only thing that I would suggest, because of the way he plays, I would suggest that he should record with a three quarter size bass instead of a full size bass."

And I remember that very vividly, and that was his input to it, but he took Dave Dexter to task for that pretty good for having the nerve to criticize anything the man played. He said nothing was wrong with his playing -- that it was the most beautiful playing he had ever heard in his life. He said it would be easier for him to record with a three quarter bass than it would -- but there's still nothing wrong with the full sized bass that he records with, but he said, as a technician, he happens to know that it would be easier for him to ...
And so the man was really unbelievable. Well, I'll tell you so much so, you were a fan of Duke Ellington's. Remember after they had left there to get 2 bass? basses.

Yeah? They had to get 2, so he must've been awful powerful, because they put him down front and you could just hear him all over the place, he had such a tone. The man was just unbelievable. Yes, we were very dear friends,
